title: Vic tops car theft, home invasion stakes
full_text:
New insurance data shows a car is stolen or broken into every 43 minutes in Victoria, while a home is broken into every two hours, dwarfing figures in the other states.
Insurance Council of Australia data to be released on Thursday reveals that there were 12,300 insurance claims for car thefts in Victoria last financial year, worth a total of $244 million - higher than all the other states combined.
The report also reveals for the first time national data on home break ins which show Victoria is the home invasion capital of the country. The state had 3900 property theft claims made last financial year worth a total of $56 million, also the highest level in the country.
Crime is shaping as a key issue for the November 28 state election, following a surge in shoplifting and violence towards staff as well as a spate drive-by shootings and arson attacks in Melbourne this year.
Neil Chatfield, the chairman of poker machine maker Aristocrat Leisure, said he had friends who were living in fear. "It started with car theft, now they are breaking into people's homes while they are sleeping." News p7
